scope: generic adult musculoskeletal animation reference; not person-specific clinical assessment
notes: CDC averages are group means with confidence intervals for the MEAN, not ranges of physiological possibility nor safe prescriptions.
Shoulder complex flexion is NOT isolated glenohumeral flexion; scapula and clavicle contribute.
Axes, zero angles and side conventions must be explicitly calibrated to each actual model; no suffix assumption.
Joint ranges vary by age, exercise, training, anthropometry, posture, load, pain and active/passive examination.
Simultaneous multi-joint configurations may collide or be infeasible even if each scalar angle is individually within a norm.
Never infer muscle excitation/force from angle; physiology and skin deformation have independent constraints.
This repository has not measured real joint angles on the reconstructed W8/V14/R120 rigs.
Exercise motion and rendering approval require measured poses, joint coordination, contact and nonpenetration across a trajectory.

population_statistics.meaning: degree-valued mean and 95% confidence interval of group mean; not physiological min/max

coupling_rules.statement: Arm elevation combines glenohumeral, scapulothoracic and clavicular motion; do not impose a single fixed 2:1 or 3:1 ratio or a fixed scapular setting phase.
Pronation/supination occur across proximal and distal radioulnar articulation; do not twist the entire forearm as a single fixed cylinder.
Knee flexion should be coupled to patellar tracking, tibiofemoral contact and restricted axial motion; do not allow unrestricted independent 3-axis rotation.
Foot-ground support involves ankle, subtalar, mid-foot and toes; ensure heel/forefoot and toe-off contact instead of only one ankle rotation.
A muscle crossing two joints can change path length when either joint moves; do not drive it solely by one angle or confuse activation with length.

acceptance.hardware_requirements: No laptop needed for cloud review; interactive anatomy correction remains separately gated
